references.text: Gideon received the name Jerubba'al (he who contends with Ba'al) after he tore down Baal's altar.
The Midianites gathered against Israel, and Gideon assembled the people to meet them in battle.
Gideon and his men attacked the Midianite camp from this position at the spring of Harod.
Joshua mentions Moreh Hill as a geographical landmark in the Jezreel Valley.
Mount Gilboa and the area around the Jezreel Valley were the site of several important battles in Israel's history.
The Philistines also camped by a spring (Aphek) before battle, using a similar military strategy to what Gideon employed.
